reading-day.markdown:
The **Day** tab is the forensic replay: *I crashed on Tuesday — what happened?*
It pairs one day's glucose chart with a chronological **Episode Log**.

## The chart

The sticky glucose curve runs the width of the day, banded by target range.
Boluses, carbs, and basal changes are marked on the timeline — every color is
paired with a shape or label so the marks read without relying on color alone.

## The Episode Log

Down the right, each **episode** the engine assembled is a card in time order: an
anchor (a meal bolus, a low, an unexplained rise), the window around it, and the
**one lever** attributed to it — its earliest actionable driver. Behaviors that
also fired are folded in as *consequences* of that lever, never stacked as
separate blame.

Click an episode to highlight its window on the chart above. That handoff — log
row ↔ chart region — is how you read *why* a moment went the way it did.

> **Open your [Day surface](app:day)** to replay a specific date.

reading-diagnose.markdown:
The **Diagnose** tab answers one question: *what should I look at first?* It is a
single ranked queue of **levers** — one honest list, tuning and behavioral
mixed, most worth-your-attention at the top.

## The rank

Each row is scored by `∛(severity × recurrence × confidence)` — how bad, how
often, how sure. A big score means a lever that hurt a lot, happened repeatedly,
and the engine is confident about. The equation sits behind the per-lever
expander; the factor bars on the card show you the three inputs at a glance.

## Setting vs. habit

Every lever is chipped **⚙ Setting** or **◈ Habit**. That flavor is a chip, never
a lane — the rank stays honest across both. What differs is where "accept" sends
you:

- **⚙ Setting** findings (basal, ISF, or I:C) flow to
  [The Plan tab](#the-plan-tab) as a proposed settings change.
- **◈ Habit** levers (late bolus, over-treated low) flow to Focus / Verify, because
  no pump setting fixes them.

## "Why so few?"

A short queue is a *good* sign, not a broken one. The tail of the surface tells
you how many opportunities the engine looked at and chose to stay quiet on, and
why — thin windows, upstream causes, near-misses under threshold. Read it before
you assume nothing's wrong.

> **Open your [Diagnose surface](app:diagnose)** to see your own ranked levers.

start-here.markdown:
This tool reads *your own* Control-IQ history and tells you where your basal,
ISF, and I:C settings might be off — and where your habits, not your settings,
are driving the highs and lows. It is **advisory**. It never touches your pump;
it hands you a specific number and the evidence behind it to take to your
clinician.

## How to read any verdict here

Every claim carries an **evidence tier**, and the tier is the first thing to
read:

- **Observed** — a hard fact from the feed (a 4.5 U bolus at 19:15, BG hitting
  58). Trust it plainly.
- **Inferred** — derived from the *shape* of the curve, so it is hedged
  ("likely rescue carbs"). Weigh it, don't bank on it.
- **Not in data** — an explicit unknown the feed can't show, flagged rather than
  guessed.

The engine would rather stay silent than assert something the feed can't
support. **Silence is a verdict**, not a gap — see [How the engine reasons](#the-pipeline).

## Where to go next

- [Reading the Diagnose surface](#reading-diagnose) — the ranked list of what to
  fix first. Start here on most days.
- [Reading a Day](#reading-day) — replay a single day when you crashed and want
  to know *why*.
- [The Plan tab](#the-plan-tab) — the suggested basal profile, and how to act on
  it with your clinician.

the-plan-tab.markdown:
The **Plan** tab is the payoff: a **suggested basal profile** you can read next to
your current one, built from what Control-IQ actually delivered during clean
windows.

## Why these numbers

For each time slot the engine takes the **median** of clean delivered basal — not
the mean. Control-IQ's clean delivery is right-skewed (a tail of corrective
basal), so the mean over-suggests; the median is the honest center. Thin slots
get a wider interval and their `n`, never a confident-looking number over three
readings.

## How to act on it

This is a **conversation starter for your clinician**, not a dose. The tool won't
change a pump setting and neither should you on its say-so alone. Bring the
suggested profile, the window it was built from, and the evidence — the clinician
makes the call.

> **Open your [Plan surface](app:plan)** to see your suggested profile.

is: A local, advisory read of your Control-IQ history. It explains your report; it does not drive your pump.
One actionable cause per episode: the earliest driver, with the other co-occurring behaviors narrated as its consequences.
Every claim is tagged Observed, Inferred, or Not-in-data, and any inference is hedged, never asserted as fact.
engine.name: Scenario engine
engine.tagline: It reads your own Control-IQ feed and names the most likely driver behind each high or low, one actionable cause at a time. It also marks what it's only inferring, or can't see at all.
wont: Won't dose for you or change a pump setting. It only suggests where to look.
Won't invent what the feed can't show. Rescue carbs are invisible on Tandem Source, so anything leaning on them is Inferred at best.
Won't pile on blame. Co-occurring behaviors collapse into one attributed lever, never a stack of separate flags.
Won't grow its vocabulary casually. The lever set and the silence taxonomy are both closed, so adding one is a deliberate act.

exposures.denominator: Scored against every meal in the window: how often a meal ran into this.
exposures.label: Meals

exposures.denominator: Scored against every low in the window: how often a low ran into this.
exposures.label: Lows

exposures.denominator: Scored against every run of back-to-back corrections.
exposures.label: Correction clusters

exposures.denominator: Scored against every unexplained high in the window.
exposures.label: Unexplained highs

levers.meaning: You bolused for a meal, but glucose still ran away high afterward. The dose covered fewer carbs than the meal actually held.
levers.recommendation: Carbs were likely undercounted — estimate higher, or split the dose for big meals.
levers.title: Carb undercount

levers.meaning: Glucose was already climbing when the meal bolus landed, so the insulin spent its first stretch just catching up to a rise already underway.
levers.recommendation: Glucose was already climbing at the dose — try bolusing ~15 min before eating.
levers.title: Late bolus

levers.meaning: The meal dose was a touch strong, so glucose dropped toward a low afterward, leaving something to walk back.
levers.recommendation: The meal dose ran glucose near-low — a slightly smaller dose may leave less to walk back.
levers.title: Meal over-delivery

levers.meaning: A low got more fast carbs than it needed and rebounded high.
levers.recommendation: The low rebounded high — follow your usual low-treatment plan and recheck in 15 min before treating again.
levers.title: Over-treated low

levers.meaning: Corrections landed back-to-back before the first had finished working, and the combined insulin overshot into a low.
levers.recommendation: Corrections stacked, then went low — give one ~1–2 h to act before adding more.
levers.title: Correction stacking

levers.meaning: A correction landed while an earlier dose was still active; together they carried you low.
levers.recommendation: A correction landed on insulin still working, then went low — give one ~1–2 h to act before adding more.
levers.title: Correction on active insulin

levers.meaning: Glucose rose with the shape of a meal but no bolus sits near it. A meal that went un-bolused, or was bolused very late.
levers.recommendation: Glucose rose like a meal with no bolus near it — bolusing (even late) keeps the peak down.
levers.title: Missed / unannounced meal

levers.meaning: You bolused for the meal, glucose climbed anyway, and a correction was needed afterward. The dose did not cover what followed. This says nothing about how many carbs the meal held — only that the dose given fell short of the outcome.
levers.recommendation: A correction was needed behind this meal dose — worth watching how often that happens before changing anything.
levers.title: Meal bolus fell short

chain.body: The engine scans your feed for anchors: a meal bolus, a low, a correction, an unexplained rise. Each is a candidate moment, not yet a judgment.
Around each anchor the engine assembles an episode: the glucose curve, the insulin on board, and every behavior that fired in the window. That's the full context of what happened.
Exactly one lever is attributed per episode: its earliest actionable driver (root-cause-by-time). Other behaviors that also tripped are narrated as consequences of that lever, not as separate causes.
When one lever recurs across episodes, it becomes a pattern with a rate ("ran away high in ~28% of your meals"), scored against how many opportunities of that kind you actually had.
chain.one_liner: The same lever, again and again.

suppression_truths.body: A single dinner can trip three detectors at once. The engine does not report three problems. It attributes the earliest actionable driver and folds the rest in as its downstream consequences. A behavior that genuinely happened can be outranked by an earlier cause and suppressed. Fewer, truer flags beat a longer list.
suppression_truths.title: One episode, one lever.

suppression_truths.body: Sometimes a behavior doesn't clear its bar. Sometimes an observable low or suspend upstream already explains the move, or a prior bolus owns the rise. In each case the engine stays silent and records why. Every quiet episode carries a reason (below). It would rather say nothing than assert something the feed can't support.
suppression_truths.title: Silence is a verdict, not a gap.

silence_reasons.body: The window was too sparse to judge, with not enough readings to say anything honest.
silence_reasons.label: Insufficient data

silence_reasons.body: The behavior plainly didn't happen: a flat slope, no stack, no correction, no low. A genuinely clean opportunity.
silence_reasons.label: No trigger

silence_reasons.body: It happened but fell short of the firing bar: the near-miss where a mis-tuned threshold hides.
silence_reasons.label: Under threshold

silence_reasons.body: An observable recent low and/or a defensive suspend explains the move. A recovery, not the behavior itself.
silence_reasons.label: Upstream cause

silence_reasons.body: The rise started from an already-high level, not from flat, so it isn't the from-flat run this detector looks for.
silence_reasons.label: Prior high baseline

silence_reasons.body: A completed carb bolus in the recent lookback already owns the rise this dose landed into. A real excursion already covered, not a late meal bolus.
silence_reasons.label: Owned by prior bolus

silence_reasons.body: A substantial announced meal at the low owns the rebound, so fast-carb treatment cannot be isolated from the meal response.
silence_reasons.label: Owned by announced meal

silence_reasons.body: The outcome never arrived inside the detector's window. The story ran past the edge of what it watches.
silence_reasons.label: Horizon expired

tiers.body: A hard fact straight from the feed, like a bolus of 10 U at 15:48, or BG hitting 64. Asserted plainly.
tiers.label: Observed

tiers.body: Shape-derived, and therefore hedged ("likely rescue carbs"). Never asserted as fact.
tiers.label: Inferred

tiers.body: An explicit unknowable, flagged as such rather than guessed.
tiers.label: Not in data

episode.spark_meta: Bolus at **18:40**, then a **slow, sustained climb**. The curve keeps rising long after the dose should have caught it.
episode.title: Dinner ran away high

worked.intro: Here's how those four stages play out on one made-up dinner. It's a walkthrough to read, not feedback on your own data.

pattern.body: This same lever recurred in ~28% of your meals this window. That rate is the pattern, scored against how many meals you actually had.

steps.text: You bolused **9.0 U** for dinner. A meal bolus is a candidate moment, so the engine flags it to watch, no judgment yet.
The engine assembles the context: the CGM curve, insulin still on board, and every behavior that fired. Glucose climbs from **132 → 247** and never turns. No correction, no low.

steps.note: A late bolus and a missed meal both also leave a rise, but the bolus was on time and sits right on the climb, so those are ruled out. One driver survives.
steps.text: The dose landed on time and glucose was flat at the meal, yet it still ran away. The likeliest driver is that the dose covered **fewer carbs than the meal held**.

verdict.body: Exactly one lever per episode. Anything else that co-occurred is folded in as a consequence, never reported as a second problem.
verdict.label: Attributed lever
verdict.title: Carb undercount
